title: Saw this clip last week but didn't have time to share it til now. 16-year-old Cavan Sullivan gets absolutely decked by 19-year-old Stuart Hawkins. What does he do? He immediately gets back up and grabs his shirt. That’s the type of fight we want from our young players! Love the mentality.
summary: Also, I just wanted to say it's so impressive to see the talent Philadelphia Union is producing in the last decade. 16 years ago, they came into the league. They had a five-point plan. They were never going to start signing big name older flashy European guys. They focused on developing the youth in the area. And it's paid dividends! I've never gotten the privilege to work for the Union. But I visited their facilities last year. Everything is super top notch and the club is so well run. I got to talk to the directors there who invited me, and they explained to me how they do things. As a sporting director myself, I've been so impressed and I can only wish to work in an environment like that. Ernst Tanner may not be the best character, he used anti-LGBTQ+ language and got suspended recently. But he has great soccer IQ and built a system that is hard to match for other MLS teams, Forget about USL, we simply don't have the financial resources and facilities they have. All in all, I think American soccer is improving thanks to clubs like the Union. I know they're not having a good season but they've been solid for years. Cavan is just the latest in their pipeline and he is not only talented, but he has the character to make it in pro soccer. When you are 16 and playing with grown men, you can't be afraid. And as you can see from this clip as one of many examples, he is not afraid of anyone or anything. We need more teams like Union in this country. Let's prioritize youth development. Teach them skillset and the tough mentality that is needed in soccer. Personally, if I were running the Union, I would bring in one or two veterans who played at the highest levels just to let them share their experiences with these young kids and to lead them. But they have their philosophy and it is helping American soccer. submitted by /u/Soccer_Professor_786 [link] [comments]

Secondo un sondaggio condotto tra fine luglio e inizio agosto dal Centro russo per la ricerca sull'opinione pubblica (Vtsiom), il 65,9% dei russi approva l'operato del presidente, una percentuale che solo pochi mesi fa si attestava all'80%. Il gradimento del leader del Cremlino rimane stagnante, dopo il crollo di 5 punti subito a luglio come effetto della grave crisi del carburante causata dagli attacchi ucraini alle raffinerie russe. Le intenzioni di voto Per quanto riguarda Russia Unita, il partito di governo legato al presidente Putin, le intenzioni di voto si attestano al 32,1%, sebbene il Cremlino sia fiducioso che la bassa affluenza alle urne gli consentirà di mantenere la maggioranza costituzionale alla Duma, la Camera bassa, il prossimo 20 settembre. Le cause del calo di popolarità Il calo della popolarità di Putin è iniziato a marzo con il blocco dei social media e il rallentamento di Internet, che hanno indignato giovani, imprenditori e militari. Secondo il Centro Levada, due terzi dei russi sono favorevoli alla cessazione delle ostilità in Ucraina e all'avvio di negoziati di pace, mentre solo un terzo degli intervistati sostiene la continuazione della guerra. La campagna elettorale In ogni caso, Putin ha deciso di guidare la campagna di Russia Unita per la prima volta dal 2007 con lo slogan "Tutto per la vittoria", un obiettivo a cui sembra subordinata ogni altra questione, ma che è ben lungi dall'essere raggiunto in Ucraina. Il precedente del 2018 Il Cremlino non si trovava in una situazione simile nei sondaggi da quando Putin decise di approvare la riforma delle pensioni praticamente in segreto, in concomitanza con la partita inaugurale dei Mondiali di calcio del 2018 in Russia. All'epoca, la popolarità di Putin crollò in meno di due mesi dall'80% al 62%, soprattutto tra l'elettorato di riferimento del Cremlino: gli over 50. L'opposizione e Yabloko Nelle elezioni del mese prossimo, la maggior parte delle figure dell'opposizione russa in esilio ha già invitato a votare per l'unico partito contrario alla guerra, Yabloko, che però oggi ha dovuto prendere le distanze da questi endorsement per timore di essere escluso dalle elezioni con l'accusa di aver beneficiato di interferenze straniere. Russia ahead of elections, declining support for Putin. AGI - Vladimir Putin, a little over six weeks before the elections to renew the Russian Parliament, continues to experience a hemorrhage of support. According to a survey conducted between late July and early August by the Russian Center for Public Opinion Research (Vtsiom), 65.9% of Russians approve of the president’s actions, a figure that just months ago stood at 80%. The approval rating of the Kremlin leader remains stagnant, after falling five points in July as a result of the serious fuel crisis caused by Ukraine's attacks on Russian refineries. Voting Intentions Regarding United Russia, the ruling party linked to President Putin, voting intentions stand at 32.1%, although the Kremlin is confident that low voter turnout will allow it to maintain its constitutional majority in the State Duma (the lower house) on September 20th. Causes of the Decline in Popularity The decline in Putin’s popularity began in March with the blocking of social media and the slowdown of Internet, which angered young people, entrepreneurs, and military personnel. According to the Levada Center, two-thirds of Russians are favorable to ending hostilities in Ukraine and initiating peace negotiations, while only one-third of those surveyed support continuing the war. The Election Campaign In any case, Putin has decided to lead United Russia’s campaign for the first time since 2007 with the slogan "Everything for Victory," a goal that seems to be subordinate to all other issues, but which is far from being achieved in Ukraine. The 2018 Precedent The Kremlin was not in a similar situation in polls since Putin decided to approve the pension reform practically in secret, coinciding with the opening match of the 2018 FIFA World Cup in Russia.
